s1.syndrome_frame: chronic, pruritic, erythematous plaque on the eyelid with lymphocytic infiltrates
salient_findings: pruritic, dark red plaque on the right upper eyelid
perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates around cystically dilated follicular infundibula
key_facts: 1-year history of a pruritic, dark red plaque on the right upper eyelid
plaque is 4 × 2-cm in size
plaque is erythematous, violaceous, indurated, and scaly with some papules
routine blood tests and biochemistry analysis were within normal limits
histopathologic examination revealed perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates
exocytosis of atypical lymphocytes into the epithelium
admixed plasma cells, eosinophils, and multinucleate giant cells
focal mild follicular mucin deposition on Alcian blue staining
lymphocytic infiltrates positive for CD3, CD4, CD5, and CD7
lymphocytic infiltrates negative for CD8, CD20, CD30, CD79a, and CD56
CD4 to CD8 cells ratio within hair follicles > 7:1
monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement was demonstrated

shortlist.label: Mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: Monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement and atypical lymphocytes in the epithelium are characteristic of this disease

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lymphocytic infiltrates positive for CD3, CD4, CD5, and CD7, and negative for CD8, CD20, CD30, CD79a, and CD56, are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of atypical lymphocytes and lymphocytic infiltrates with a CD4 to CD8 cells ratio > 7:1 suggests this possibility

shortlist.label: Lymphocytic infiltrate of Jessner
shortlist.why_kept: Perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates and the presence of plasma cells, eosinophils, and multinucleate giant cells could be seen in this condition

shortlist.label: Cutaneous lymphoid hyperplasia
shortlist.why_kept: The clinical presentation and histopathologic findings, including lymphocytic infiltrates and follicular mucin deposition, could be consistent with this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The presence of a long-standing pruritic plaque with histopathologic findings of perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates, exocytosis of atypical lymphocytes, and a high CD4 to CD8 ratio, along with monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement, are characteristic features of mycosis fungoides.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: Too broad, as mycosis fungoides is a specific type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with papular lesions that resolve with scarring, not a single plaque

rejected.label: Lymphocytic infiltrate of Jessner
rejected.why: Usually lacks atypical lymphocytes and monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement

rejected.label: Cutaneous lymphoid hyperplasia
rejected.why: Does not typically show monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement or the same degree of atypia
